as_told.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson debunk of Apollo 17 sightings

plain: During the Apollo Moon missions, some photos show small blue lights in the sky, and astronaut Buzz Aldrin reported seeing flashes of light inside the cabin. A skeptic writer named Michael Shermer says an astronomer, Avi Loeb, explains both as cosmic rays, fast particles from space hitting the camera or the eye, and Shermer thinks he is right. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani also credits Loeb, but ties the idea only to a trio of blue lights in photos from Apollo 17, a later mission. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says instead that the astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson put the Apollo 17 lights down to cosmic rays and called it case closed. The point of the explanation is that the lights would then need no unusual cause.
